library_preparation_preflight.summary: google-oauth-client needs a JsonFactory implementation to reach its main paths: TokenResponse parsing, TokenRequest.execute, and the AuthorizationCodeFlow and credential flows. Its transitive google-http-client dependency has none; the JSON factories ship as separate artifacts. No Docker image is needed.

deterministic_setup.reason: Supplies GsonFactory, a JsonFactory/JsonObjectParser backend. Version 1.42.3 matches the google-http-client version that google-oauth-client 1.35.0 depends on. A google-http-client-gson test already exists in the repo, at version 1.42.2.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Tests should run offline with no environment variables or system properties. Use an in-process HttpTransport: subclass HttpTransport and LowLevelHttpRequest/LowLevelHttpResponse, or use a local com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer on localhost. Do not use MockHttpTransport, because it is in the google-http-client test artifact and not in the main jar. Cover these areas: TokenRequest subclasses (AuthorizationCodeTokenRequest, RefreshTokenRequest, ClientCredentialsTokenRequest, PasswordTokenRequest), TokenResponse and TokenErrorResponse parsing via GsonFactory, AuthorizationCodeFlow with MemoryDataStoreFactory, Credential, ClientParametersAuthentication and BasicAuthentication, AuthorizationRequestUrl and AuthorizationCodeRequestUrl, and IdTokenVerifier/IdTokenResponse. Avoid the extras artifacts (the servlet, Jetty, Jackson and Java 6 modules) and LocalServerReceiver, which is not part of this artifact. Avoid anything that opens a browser.
risks: Without a JsonFactory, tests are likely to cover only URL, parameter and builder classes, so the reflective JSON paths would be missed.
The google-http-client-gson version must be 1.42.3 so the resolved google-http-client does not drift from what the library resolves.
I did not run the Gradle resolution, so the transitive version is taken from memory of the library's POM and should be confirmed locally.
